newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam rejects conditional help from Vatican.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam rejects conditional help from Vatican.

text.p: Vietnam said on Saturday it had told a visiting Vatican delegation it was not interested in help from foreign organisations or countries if there were strings attached.

A statement in the English-language Vietnam News said papal envoy Archbishop Claudio Celli had offered help with health, education and agriculture during talks with government officials in Hanoi over the past week.
It did not detail the proposal but said bluntly: "Vietnam welcomes all investment and help from other countries and international organisations if it is unconditional."

The statement was Hanoi's first comment on a series of meetings over the past week which church officials said were aimed at chipping away at the frost in a troubled relationship between the Holy See and Vietnam's communist government.
Archbishop Celli said in an interview on Thursday the visit had succeeded in reopening dialogue which had been stalled for the past 18 months, but he indicated meagre progress in other areas.
Hanoi has eased tight controls on religious freedoms in recent years, but relations with the Holy See have floundered over a range of differences, some of which are fundamental.
Most of Vietnam's 75 million population is Buddhist, but its estimated seven million Catholic community is one of the largest in East Asia.

Religious commentators say that in addition to differences over dogma, Hanoi is wary of a church which is seen as having had a role in the collapse of communism in the Soviet Union and Eastern Europe.
